title: CBC/Radio-Canada as a 5th-generation warfare information vector — OSINT dossier
legal_standard: Every FACT cites a primary or on-record government/corporate source. INFERENCE labels are analytical hypotheses, not court findings. 'Genocide' framing on this site refers to the TENET5 Article II map of government policy outcomes (MAID, conditions of life, etc.) — not a criminal conviction of CBC personnel.

thesis.short: A state-funded national broadcaster whose budget is set by the government it covers is, by structure, an information-domain asset. Under a 5GW lens, that asset can shape consent, stigmatize dissent, and normalize policies that harm population cohorts — while taxpayers fund the amplifier.
thesis.5gw_definition: Fifth-generation warfare prioritizes perception, narrative, legitimacy, and cognitive effects over kinetic force. Control of trusted information channels is a primary battlespace.

vector_mechanisms.name: Budget dependency
vector_mechanisms.inference: Annual appropriation creates structural incentive to avoid sustained adversarial coverage of the funding principal (Cabinet / governing party).
vector_mechanisms.falsifiable_by: Multi-year adversarial investigative series on governing-party scandals that measurably reduce CBC appropriation without retaliation narrative.

vector_mechanisms.name: Appointment channel
vector_mechanisms.inference: Governor-in-Council appointment of Board/CEO is a soft-power control surface even under 'arm's length' rhetoric.
vector_mechanisms.falsifiable_by: Statutory independent appointment regime with multipartisan parliamentary confirmation and transparent merit scores.

vector_mechanisms.name: Trust brand as force multiplier
vector_mechanisms.inference: Even declining trust remains high relative to many private brands; residual trust multiplies narrative effects of framing choices (what is 'extremism', who is 'fringe', which deaths are 'policy success').
vector_mechanisms.falsifiable_by: Content audits showing equal adversarial intensity toward all major parties and equal framing of state-caused harm clusters.

vector_mechanisms.name: Ecosystem subsidy stack
vector_mechanisms.inference: CBC is the apex state broadcaster inside a wider taxpayer-subsidized news stack; combined effect is a managed information environment, not a free market of ideas.
vector_mechanisms.falsifiable_by: Independent outlets without subsidy access outranking state-funded brands on reach and trust for national policy news.

vector_mechanisms.name: Emergency / crisis narrative authority
vector_mechanisms.inference: Heritage proposals to expand emergency-comms role + high appropriation make CBC a preferred amplifier during Emergencies Act-class events and public-health crises.
vector_mechanisms.falsifiable_by: Crisis coverage scorecards showing systematic platforming of rights-critical experts equal to government briefers.

tax_dollar_to_harm_chain.title: Tax dollars → information environment → policy consent → population harm clusters
tax_dollar_to_harm_chain.honest_scope: This chain is a systems model. It does not allege that every CBC journalist intends harm. It maps how public money funds the dominant narrative layer around policies TENET5 already documents with primary health/AG/Hansard sources.

steps.label: Taxpayer extraction
steps.content: Federal taxes fund Consolidated Revenue → annual CBC appropriation (~$1.3–1.4B class) + wider journalism subsidies.

steps.label: Institutional amplifier
steps.content: CBC operates multi-platform news (TV, radio, digital) with national reach and public-service brand legitimacy.

steps.label: Framing power
steps.content: Story selection, expert choice, language (safety vs liberty, compassion vs eugenics critique, protest vs occupation) sets the Overton window for voters and MPs.

steps.label: Consent for hard policies
steps.content: MAID expansion, Emergencies Act use, demographic/immigration volume without capacity, procurement opacity — each requires a media climate that treats dissent as marginal.

steps.label: Population outcomes (TENET5 record)
steps.content: Mapped on-site: MAID death totals (Health Canada), opioid deaths, housing/healthcare capacity collapse indicators, veteran MAID cases, Indigenous conditions. These are policy-outcome facts; the media vector question is whether state-funded narrative suppressed timely adversarial scrutiny.

trudeau_era_anchors.media_question: Did state-funded outlets frame expansion primarily as compassion while under-weighting disability-rights and veteran-pressure cases?
Did coverage prioritize government threat framing over Charter/proportionality scrutiny during freezing of accounts?
Did coverage lag primary inquiry findings that implicated sitting MPs / diaspora intimidation?
Did outlets receiving labour tax credits / LJI normalize subsidy as 'saving journalism' without conflict-of-interest banners?

open_questions: Content-analysis sample: MAID expansion coverage ratio of disability-rights voices vs government spokespeople on CBC digital (2020–2024).
